title: A shift that moved outside the 60-day-back/366-day-forward sync window is indistinguishable from a deleted shift, and the confirm screen states it as certain
where: index.html:1545-1576 (icsPlanFromExisting removal logic, esp. `if(!inWindow(rec.dateKey)) return;`), 826-864 (parseICSSchedule drops out-of-window events before the caller ever sees them), 3828-3834 (IcsImportSheet: "Removing … — gone from your calendar feed.")
detail: `parseICSSchedule` silently drops any VEVENT outside [today-60d, today+366d] (`droppedWindow`, 864) — the caller never learns the event still exists at a new date outside that range. `icsPlanFromExisting`'s removal pass then treats "this icsUid wasn't seen in the fresh parse" as "deleted from the calendar" as long as the *previously stored* dateKey is inside the window (1558-1566) — it has no way to tell "deleted" apart from "moved to a date the current fetch window doesn't cover." The confirm sheet then asserts, unconditionally, that the listed shifts are "gone from your calendar feed" (3832-3834) with no hedge.
failure: A shift that was correctly imported near-term gets rescheduled in the source calendar to more than 366 days out (e.g. a hospital or travel-nurse contract that publishes far-future dates) or corrected to a date more than 60 days in the past. The next sync no longer sees that UID in-window, proposes it under "Removing … gone from your calendar feed," and if the user (trusting the app's own confident wording) taps Confirm, `icsConfirmImport` permanently deletes a shift that was never actually cancelled — losing real logged hours/pay-type data with no undo.
fix: Either widen/soften the removal claim when the shift's own recorded date is near a window boundary, or track that the UID was seen previously and simply skip removal (leave it stored, unflagged) when its own current window straddles a boundary, and change the confirm copy from an assertion ("gone from your calendar feed") to a hedge (e.g. "no longer appears in the synced window").
